title: Ayako
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In occupied post-war Japan, the landowning Tenge family loses its estates to land reform. When young Ayako witnesses secret murders by an elder brother who works as an agent for the US occupiers, the family locks her in an underground cellar to hide that crime and its own incestuous secrets; she stays there for over two decades while the country changes above her. Osamu Tezuka's adult drama follows the family's collapse.
life_message: No clear good life is held up; the story shows how a family that sacrifices a child to protect its honor and secrets destroys itself.

content.note: Political murders, an assassin and spy plot, gangsters (Wikipedia, Manga Bookshelf; MU Murder/s, Assassin/s).
A child imprisoned underground for over twenty years; dark, sobering tone (Wikipedia, Manga Bookshelf; MU Dark Ambience, Captive/s).
Incest is central: the patriarch fathers Ayako with his son's wife; sexual abuse of Ayako; nudity (Wikipedia, Manga Bookshelf; MU Incest, Rape, Nudity). Described as stark, not graphic (to verify).
Ayako's isolation and fear of the outside world; emotional abuse and mental breakdown (Wikipedia; MU Emotional Abuse, Mental Breakdown).
Crimes and abuse shown as destructive; not presented for imitation.

dominant: Critique of patriarchal family honor; post-war upheaval; naturalism

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Family hides crimes to protect its name, imprisoning Ayako (Wikipedia, Manga Bookshelf).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Patriarch's rule is absolute in the household.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Domineering patriarch over sons and women (Manga Bookshelf).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Old feudal order versus occupation reforms; story critiques the old order.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival and status dominate the family's choices.

folkways.japan: Set amid post-war land reform and US occupation; shows the decline of the rural landowning ie (household) system and its honor norms, which the story critiques.

delivery.evidence: Manga Bookshelf calls it heavily symbolic and uneven but not preachy; message carried by the family's collapse.

personified.ideology: Japan caught between old order and US occupiers

delivery.note: Tezuka criticizes both the old Japanese social order and American occupation efforts, per the review.

winners_losers: The Tenge family destroys itself; Ayako is the chief victim; sympathy rests with the imprisoned and powerless, not with patriarchal honor.
